title: GPU microregion stewardship and lazy coalescence playbook
creator: Priya Nair
description: Introduce a low-disruption allocation and background coalescence strategy for the KV cache that targets fragmentation hotspots while preserving tail latency guarantees for continuous batching workloads. The approach combines small per-GPU 'microregions' (16KB-256KB windows) with an indirection remap table, occupancy heatmaps, and opportunistic lazy coalescence executed in bounded background windows to reduce long-lived fragmentation and tenant-induced noise.
motivation: We observe persistent fragmentation on long-lived dedicated instances and private deployments where heterogeneous batch shapes and multi-tenant churn produce many small free holes. This increases eviction churn, forces conservative preemption, and ultimately raises p99/loss-of-throughput for high-concurrency routes. Existing global compaction triggers either stall the runtime or move excessive memory, causing regressions in latency-sensitive traffic. We need a targeted, low-latency-safe mechanism to reclaim usable contiguous regions without large synchronous copies.
design_decisions: Microregion granularity: use adaptive microregion sizes (default 64KB) chosen per-device based on cudaMalloc fragmentation profile and typical KV object size distribution.
Indirection remap table: maintain per-GPU remap table allowing logical slot -> physical microregion mapping so small relocations swap remap entries instead of copying large contiguous pages.
Occupancy heatmaps: track hot/free counters per-microregion with decay; heatmap windows drive selection of candidate neighbors for coalescing.

Lazy coalescence: perform defragmentation in bounded background tasks that only touch microregions when occupancy skew exceeds a threshold, with a strict CPU/GPU time budget per cycle to avoid latency impact.
Tenant quarantine: avoid relocating microregions that contain pinned tenant state unless tenant QoS permits or a safe handoff via staged KV replay is possible.
Fallback path: if remap table capacity or relocation budget is exhausted, fall back to current slab replacement + proactive eviction path.
Telemetry-first rollout: gate heuristic thresholds behind feature flag and surface new metrics (microregion_free_runs, remap_ops, background_coalesce_time) to Console before wide rollout.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (prototype): implement remap table and microregion allocator in a runtime dev branch; add APIs to pin/unpin microregions; basic heatmap counters (in GPU shared mem + sampled increments).

Phase 2 (engine): add lazy coalescer worker that scans high-skew microregion groups, does small intra-GPU relocations via ephemeral copy buffers, and atomically swaps remap entries. Ensure CUDA streams sync points keep inference streams non-blocking.
Phase 3 (safety): implement tenant quarantine checks, budgeted coalescence scheduler, and metrics emission.
Phase 4 (dogfood): enable on internal dedicated clusters, collect fragmentation metrics and latency regressions across a mixture of batch sizes and tenant skews.
Phase 5 (canary): enable behind runtime-flag for 10% of production traffic; observe p50/p95/p99 and eviction counts for 48h before broader rollout.
testing_plan: Unit tests: remap table correctness, atomic swap invariants, boundary conditions for microregion splits/merges.
Integration tests: multi-stream resharding with synthetic KV workloads that emulate LLM inference (varying seq-len/batch shapes), assert no blocking stalls and correctness under preemption.
Stress tests: long-running churn test (7 days) with tenant create/destroy and skew injection; assert fragmentation metric monotonic improvement and no p99 regressions.
Fuzz: random allocation/free patterns to detect ABA or race conditions in remap swaps.
Performance: compare token throughput and p99 latency against current allocator for representative models (Llama2-13B and a 70B variant) on each GPU class (A100, H100).
rollout_plan: Collect baseline telemetry for 7 days across dedicated and private fleets.
Enable feature-flagged runtime on internal clusters and run workload mix A/B for 72 hours.
Canary 10% of production traffic for 48 hours; if no regressions, ramp to 50% then 100% over a week.
Expose Console dashboard 'Microregion Steward' for SRE/Platform and add automatic alerts for remap_ops_rate spikes or coalescer_time > budget.
If at any step latency regressions > 10% p99 or unplanned evictions increase, revert flag and capture full heap+trace dump.
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation metric: median free_run_length increases by >= 2x on target clusters within 72 hours compared to baseline.
Latency: p99 token latency no worse than 5% vs baseline during background coalescence activity.
Eviction reduction: per-minute eviction count decreases by >= 15% on sustained workloads with high tenant churn.
Operational: no JVM/segment faults observed; remap_ops and coalescer_time metrics available in Console and reason codes for forced fallbacks.
Rollback safety: feature flag disables all background activity and reverts remap table to identity mapping without requiring node restart.
risks: Remap table contention: high-frequency remaps could become a bottleneck under extreme churn — mitigate with sharded remap locks and batch-swap semantics.
GPU copy overhead: ephemeral relocations can consume bandwidth; enforce strict time/bandwidth budget and prefer locality-aware coalesces.
Correctness hazards: atomic remap swaps must be free of ABA; require versioned remap entries with guarded CAS.
Observability gaps: without early telemetry the feature could regress silently; block rollout until metrics are present.
Complexity: increased code surface in hot path; plan dedicated code reviews and a small feature team to own maintenance.
notes: This playbook focuses on reducing medium-granularity fragmentation (tens to hundreds of KB) which we see as the dominant contributor to eviction spikes for mixed batch workloads. It intentionally avoids full-page compaction to preserve latency SLAs. Will coordinate with Kernel and CUDA teams on efficient device-to-device copy primitives.
